ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2.
The sequence s has exactly n minus 1 entries.
Each entry of s is either plus 1 or minus 1.
The tuple a is a permutation of {1, 2, ..., n}, so all entries are distinct and each integer from 1 to n appears exactly once.
The inequality si times (a(i+1) - ai) greater than 0 means ai+1 is greater than ai when si is plus 1, and ai+1 is less than ai when si is minus 1.
The constraint must hold for every index i from 1 to n minus 1.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each integer n at least 2, among all length n minus 1 sequences of plus or minus 1, determine exactly which sign patterns maximize the number of permutations of 1 through n whose consecutive differences have the prescribed signs.
quantifier_order: First fix an integer n with n at least 2.
Then range over all sign sequences s of length n minus 1.
For a given s, count all permutations a of {1, 2, ..., n} satisfying the adjacent sign constraints for every i from 1 to n minus 1.
Finally, for each n, identify which sequences s maximize this count.

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

payload.proof_nl:
Fix n at least 2 and a sign sequence s=(s_1,...,s_{n-1}) with each s_i in {+1,-1}. Let A_s be the set of permutations a=(a_1,...,a_n) of {1,...,n} such that s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0 for every i=1,...,n-1. By definition, |A_s|=f(s). Similarly define A_{-s}.

Define a map T on permutations of {1,...,n} by
T(a_1,...,a_n)=(n+1-a_1,...,n+1-a_n).
Because the map x -> n+1-x is a bijection from {1,...,n} to itself, T sends permutations of {1,...,n} to permutations of {1,...,n}. Also T is an involution, since applying it twice gives back the original permutation:
T(T(a_1,...,a_n))=(a_1,...,a_n).
Hence T is a bijection on the set of all permutations of {1,...,n}.

Now take any a=(a_1,...,a_n) in A_s, and write b=T(a). For each i=1,...,n-1 we have
b_{i+1}-b_i=(n+1-a_{i+1})-(n+1-a_i)=-(a_{i+1}-a_i).
Therefore
(-s_i)(b_{i+1}-b_i)=(-s_i)(-(a_{i+1}-a_i))=s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0.
So b satisfies the defining inequalities for A_{-s}, and thus T(a) is in A_{-s}.

Conversely, if b is in A_{-s}, the same calculation applied to T(b) shows that T(b) is in A_s, because T is its own inverse. Therefore T restricts to a bijection from A_s onto A_{-s}.

Since bijective finite sets have the same cardinality, |A_s|=|A_{-s}|. Equivalently, f(s)=f(-s). This is exactly the claimed statement.
payload.role_in_assembly: This symmetry reduces the analysis of patterns starting with -1 to the already solved case of patterns starting with +1, and it also shows the two alternating maximizers have equal value.

payload.statement_nl: Let n be an integer at least 2, and let s=(s_1,...,s_{n-1}) with each s_i in {+1,-1}. Define -s=(-s_1,...,-s_{n-1}). Let f(s) be the number of permutations a=(a_1,...,a_n) of {1,...,n} such that s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0 for every 1 <= i <= n-1. Then f(s)=f(-s).

result_payload.reason: The proof gives a complete involutive bijection between permutations counted by f(s) and those counted by f(-s), via coordinatewise complement a_i ↦ n+1-a_i. It correctly verifies preservation of the permutation property, computes the sign reversal on adjacent differences, and shows the map is its own inverse, hence bijective. This exactly proves f(s)=f(-s) with no semantic drift and no reliance on forbidden or undeclared dependencies.
